note: Researcher-proposed follow-ups. A human promotes one to questions.json to make it runnable.

tasks.experiment: mc_calibration with gamma=0 for both classes, larger n_sims, different seed
tasks.question: Does the day-clustered Wald test hold nominal size with more sims (e.g. several hundred)?
tasks.why: n=16 cannot distinguish 12.5% from 5% reliably; the cluster rejection rate and coverage need tighter bounds.

tasks.experiment: mc_calibration with level_sd varied, still gamma=0
tasks.question: How does robust and cluster size vary with level_sd (day-level shock size) and with the number of event windows?
tasks.why: Inference is identified by event windows, not trades; this checks how the SE understatement scales.

tasks.question: Which inference procedure does the pre-registration specify for criterion (2), and does the code path used for the real data apply day-clustered or placebo-based inference?
tasks.why: The trade-level robust test is shown oversized here, so criterion (2) must not rely on it alone.

tasks.experiment: Run the runner on one real ticker twice (with and without fix_acceptance_tz) and diff events.csv and the gamma estimates. Count this as an extra spec in the forking-paths ledger.
tasks.question: After wiring fix_acceptance_tz into run_real.py and run_layer1.py (per the TODO text), how many events move by 4-5 h per ticker, and does the sign or significance of either gamma change?
tasks.why: Quantifies the impact of the A1-5 gap on the reported long-run effects and on the placebo and offset-scan criteria.

tasks.question: Do pool_events.py, peer_pilot.py and edgar_census.py parse acceptance times via edgar.parse_acceptance, and do they apply the per-filer shift?
tasks.why: I did not read these scripts, so other runners may share the A1-5 gap.

tasks.experiment: mc_calibration with gamma=0 for both classes, n_sims>=200, different seed
tasks.question: Does the day-cluster (or day-block) Wald test hold nominal size with a larger number of simulations (e.g. >=200)?
tasks.why: 16 sims cannot establish size for the cluster test; 0.125 is inconclusive.

tasks.experiment: mc_calibration null runs with level_sd varied (including 0)
tasks.question: Is placebo randomization (criterion 3) correctly sized under the null with day-level shocks, and how do rejection rates vary with level_sd?
tasks.why: Pre-registered gate relies on placebo p-values, which respect day-level dependence by construction if placebos are assigned at the event-window level.

tasks.question: Check how the pre-registered joint Wald statistic is computed in the repo (trade-level vs day-clustered covariance) and whether the registered protocol allows a clustered correction before holdout use.
tasks.why: If the registered criterion 2 uses the oversized robust test, the gate is anti-conservative; any change must be a documented protocol amendment, not post hoc tuning.

tasks.question: Re-run the same null, level_sd=0 control with a much larger n_sims (e.g. >=200) so the rejection rate has a usable confidence interval.
tasks.why: 16 sims cannot separate 5% from 15% size, so the machinery-bug question is still open.

tasks.experiment: mc_calibration with gamma=0, level_sd>0, same seeds
tasks.question: Run the paired contrast with the same seeds and level_sd>0, comparing robust SE to the empirical SD, to quantify the day-shock inflation relative to this control.
tasks.why: The ratio of mean SE to empirical SD (about 1.0 here) versus the shocked case is the direct evidence for the day-shock explanation.

tasks.question: Check how the cluster-by-day covariance estimator treats the small number of event windows, for example whether a small-sample correction is applied.
tasks.why: Cluster SE for scheduled is slightly below the empirical SD, and the cluster rate is the higher of the two.

tasks.question: Apply TODO A1-5 in run_real.py and run_layer1.py, then compare eff_ns, event counts and gamma against the current run for the same ticker.
tasks.why: Quantifies how much the missing per-filer shift changes the headline result.

tasks.question: How many census filers have an all-pre-market filing pattern, so that decide_shift in auto mode cannot detect a shift? Compare auto against mode='shifted' on the 18 Oct census.
tasks.why: Shows whether the false-negative case in edgar.decide_shift occurs on real filers.

tasks.question: Check scripts/pull_databento.py, fetch_8k_pages.py, peer_pilot.py and monte_carlo_bias.py, plus the autoresearch/ harness, for silent defects.
tasks.why: These were skimmed or outside this audit's reading budget.

tasks.why: Citations need fetched pages and exact quotes. Rambaldi et al. and Yang et al. are the closest disconfirming candidates.

tasks.why: The method could be adopted or benchmarked, for example a non-causal pre-event kernel as a placebo or pre-trend check. It also bears on criterion (5), the offset-scan peak.

tasks.question: Read the Yang et al. 2018 multivariate Hawkes sentiment paper and check how it handles news timestamps and look-ahead.
tasks.why: It is the nearest text-plus-point-process work and could force a softer novelty claim.
